To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the restricted symport P system with multiple number of symbols and multiple number or rules (objects), or the restricted symport system with multiple number or membranes and multiple number or symbols, or the restricted antiport P system with single number of membranes and multiple number (objects) accept all context-sensitive languages, and that the restricted sym-port/antiport P-systems with single number of symbols and single number of membranes accept all regular languages.

(i) for the first time in the P systems literature, context-sensitive languages are characterized syntactically by symport/anti-port P systems; and (ii) there are infinite hierarchies in computational power of the restricted symport / antiport P systems with respect to both the number of symbols and the number of membranes.

(i) the restricted symport P system with two membranes accepts exactly the binary context-sensitive languages (and thus, it is a "syntactic characterization" of the binary context-sensitive language class); and (ii) the restricted sym port P system with three membranes accepts all binary context-sensitive languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the computational power of symport/ antiport P systems with restricted features.
the following question: How powerful is a symport/anti-port P system with m ≥ 1 and s ≥ 2, when both m and s are fixed?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the restricted symport P system with two membranes and multiple objects is the first P system model that can accept CSLs, and that this model is strictly weaker than the symport/anti-port P system with two symbols and two membranes, which is known to be equivalent to the unrestricted symport/anti- port P system with two objects and two membranes.

the restricted symport P systems with multiple symbols and multiple membranes can accept all binary CSL languages, and that the restricted symports P systems with multiple membranes can accept the recursively enumerable languages.
the restricted symport P systems are the most powerful among the symport/anti-port P systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the symport/anti-port communication mode is not powerful enough to accept CSLs.

the restricted symport P systems (with antiport rules allowed) can be used to characterize all the recursively enumerable sets (and some other classes of languages), while the symport P systems with antiport rules forbidden cannot characterize any class of languages beyond the regular languages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the restricted symport and antiport rules, in conjunction with membrane division, can be used to obtain characterizations of formal language classes.
the symport/anti-port communication mechanism, when suitably constrained, is a powerful tool for capturing the power of formal language models.
the restricted symport P systems with multiple objects and antiports are a very powerful model for accepting CSLs.
